topic: Breath series 5b: Diaphragmatic breathing, breathe-along short version (off grid)
caption:
Got one minute? Six slow belly breaths, in and out through your nose, paced for you.

Rest one hand on your belly. Breathe in through your nose for about four seconds and let your belly rise, then slowly out through your nose for about six. There's no magic ratio, so go at a pace that feels easy.

Keep it gentle. If you feel light-headed or tingly, go back to your usual breathing. If you have COPD or another lung condition, check with your doctor first: in some studies of people with COPD, deep belly breathing made breathing harder work.

The practice-only version of our belly breathing Reel. The full version, with the research behind it, is on our profile @equal_psychology.

Save this for another time.

Research:

Holland, A. E. et al. (2012). Breathing exercises for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Cochrane Database Syst Rev, 2012(10), CD008250. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD008250.pub2
